newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans flock to big stores as shop hours extended.
newsitem.headline: Germans flock to big stores as shop hours extended.

text.p: As major store managers counted the takings on Saturday from Germany's first day of longer shopping hours, their customers appeared to have given the move an enthusiastic thumbs-up.

Germany's biggest department store, Karstadt's KaDeWe in Berlin, said it had done around 20 percent of its trade between 6.30 p.m. and 8 p.m. on Friday -- the day that new shopping hours came into force.
Frankfurt's Zeil, the highest-turnover shopping street in the country, remained busy until closing time.

Joseph Stoffer, the manager of Berlin's new luxury department store Galeries Lafayette said his customers had been enthusiastic about the chance to shop until 8 p.m. from Monday to Friday rather than see the store close at 6.30.
"If this demand continues, we'll be taking on extra staff," he said.
The liberalisation of shopping hours amended laws passed in the 1950s and took several years of often bitter debate to push through parliament.

Labour unions and small shopkeepers have opposed the reform, arguing it would not boost turnoer but only draw business away from smaller shops to the large city-centre stores which can afford to take on more staff.

A glance around some of the deserted shops away from the Zeil in Frankfurt appeared to bear this out, although one jeweller reported she had done a quarter of her day's business between 6 p.m. and 7 p.m.
